title: The scary first year
topic: Falls, and the time to wait

steps.title: A fall is not the end
steps.body: You invest €5,000. After one bad year, it is worth €4,000. Swings like this are called [[volatility]]. A fall becomes a real loss when you sell during it. If you can wait, the price has time to recover. But nobody can promise that it will. How long your money can wait is your [[time-horizon]].

steps.prompt: After a fall, the price must rise more than it fell to get back to the start. Move the slider to find the loss that needs a rise of 25%.

output.label: Rise needed to get back to the start

steps.prompt: Imagine you put €5,000 in a fund. After one bad year, it is worth €4,000. What do you do? Choose, and see the result after 17 years.

choices.label: Sell now and keep the money as cash
choices.ending: At the end, you have €5,100. Selling turned a fall on paper into a real loss. The cash then barely kept up with prices.

choices.label: Keep the fund and check it less often
choices.ending: At the end, you have €11,800, after a hard first year. In this example, the market recovered. Past returns do not tell you what the next 17 years will bring.

choices.label: Never invest the €5,000
choices.ending: At the end, you have €6,400. The value never fell, but it grew less. You get less worry for less growth.

steps.prompt: True or false: a fund that lost 20% needs a 20% rise to get back to the start.
steps.explanation: False. €4,000 × 1.25 = €5,000. The rise starts from the smaller amount, so it must be bigger than the fall. It needs 25%. This is how a [[drawdown]] works.

steps.prompt: Why does a 20% fall hurt money for a child's studies in 17 years less than money for next month's rent?
options: The money for studies has 17 years to recover, and nobody needs to sell it now
A 20% fall is a small loss
steps.explanation: Rent money would have to be sold at the low price. Money that can wait has time for the price to recover, but nothing guarantees that it will.

steps.title: A bad year for your account
steps.body: Your investment account holds **{depotTotal}**. After a 20% fall, it would be worth about **{depotAfterFall}**. To get back to today's value, it would then need a rise of 25%.

scenes.title: One bad year
scenes.desc: Prices go up and down. These swings are called [[volatility]]. A fall is only a real loss if you sell during it. How long your money can wait is your [[time-horizon]].
